generator: Blender 4.2 Cycles (CPU, OIDN), numpy-groomed hair curves; see scratchpad/blender/sprites.py

body.notes: column k is pre-rotated to screen angle k/angles*PI (body axis (cos, sin), y down) and lit by the fixed screen light; rotate by the residual (<= half a bucket). Each cell is a window cut from a continuous rendered fur tube: |along| <= along*R*(1-(|across|/1.5R)^4)^0.25 with a +-feather*R smoothstep cross-fade, the sides keep the real silhouette fuzz (fuzz = reach beyond R). Stamp it every ~0.3R (dense 0.075R stamping only shows a thin rim slice of each cell and smears the fur into streaks). Straight alpha.

head.generator: Blender 4.2 Cycles (CPU, OIDN), numpy-groomed hair curves; head v3 = plush head in profile after the client photo; dev/blender/head_v3.py + head_v3_pack.py

grade.notes: gain_srgb (after the exposure) makes head x head_tint (snake.js HEAD_TINT) equal the body.webp pink at the neck (x -1.0..-0.45 R) under the same light; residual mean [0.6, -0.6, -0.6] sRGB

eye.measured: centre + visible radius (dark bead incl. glint, fur ring excluded) on the 2x render of cell 0
eye.per_bucket_note: every cell is [1] = draw as stored (snake.js headPick mirrors a cell only for [0]); the single bead is centres[0]. Unlike v2, the values do not index centres.
eye.notes: one glossy bead, baked in every cell on the side facing the camera; centre (x, y) in R, cell frame (x forward, image y down = -u). Never flipped (engine headPick: per_bucket [1]).

shape.source: client plush photo, side view (outer fur edge traced by the site session)
shape.frame: units of R; x forward from the head point; u across, + = jaw side, - = brow side; cell image y = -u (jaw toward -y, brow toward +y)

brow_neck_shoulder.notes: deviation from the traced brow, x < x_join only: the brow is widened to the body fur edge (|u| = u) over [x_back1, x_front], tapering back to the traced brow by x_back0 and rounding into it by x_join (C1 Hermite). It covers the front end of snake.js's first body stamp (0.3 R behind the head point, lens cut at x ~ +0.06 R), which showed as a square tab above the traced 1.14 R brow. Body-style grooming on that band. See dev/blender/head_v3_spec.py BROW_SHOULDER.

shape.notes: fit_R on the packed cell 0, x >= -1.0 R, alpha >= 0.5 edge vs the target (outer_fur_edge + brow_neck_shoulder): brow/jaw = signed normal deviation target -> edge (+ = outside); edge_to_target = distance edge -> nearest target point (max / mean / p95; max includes stray fur strands); brow_vs_traced_in_shoulder = the brow vs the traced polyline inside the shoulder. See dev/blender/head_v3_check.py

scale.notes: rh_ref = ref_R * head_scale, so the engine draws the cell at R / ref_R with the origin on the path's head point

head.notes: cell b at column b % cols, row floor(b / cols); head points +x, lit for heading th = b/buckets*2PI with the fixed screen key light (rotate the cell by th about origin). Neck fade baked into alpha (x in neck_fade_R); pink fur runs into the body (no collar). Eye baked (see eye). No tongue (engine draws it from tongue_base_R). Straight alpha.

cap.notes: furry ball of radius rc_ref px with body-scale fur (scale by rc/rc_ref).
